skill.name: mcp-builder
skill.description: Guide for planning, building, and evaluating Model Context Protocol servers in TypeScript or Python. It covers tool design, schemas, transports, error handling, and evaluation workflows.
skill.summary: Build and evaluate MCP servers with practical TypeScript and Python guidance.
skill.author: YYH211

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation false positives: placeholder URLs, example API keys, Markdown backticks, and TypeScript template literals. The runnable evaluation harness has two real medium risks: it launches user-selected MCP commands and sends tool outputs to Anthropic. No prompt injection attempt or hardcoded live secret was found.

remediation.issue: Evaluation data can be sent to Anthropic.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning and optional redaction step before sending MCP tool outputs to the model provider.

remediation.issue: Stdio evaluation can run a user-selected local command.
remediation.suggestion: Document that commands must be trusted, avoid shell wrappers, and consider an allowlist for automated use.

remediation.issue: Documentation uses placeholder secrets and tokens in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders clearly fake and add guidance to use least-privilege, revocable credentials for evaluations.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Harness Sends Tool Outputs to Anthropic
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation loop sends user tasks and MCP tool results through Anthropic messages. Sensitive tool outputs could leave the local environment during evaluation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly calls client.messages.create and appends serialized tool results into follow-up messages. This confirms third-party processing of evaluation data.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Harness Launches User-Selected Commands
semantic_findings.description: The stdio evaluation path accepts a command, arguments, and environment values, then starts the selected MCP server process. This is expected but risky with untrusted input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI exposes command and args, and MCPConnectionStdio passes them into StdioServerParameters. There is no shell string injection, but it still runs local processes.

content.value_statement: MCP server builders need clear patterns for tools, transports, schemas, and testing. This skill provides practical guidance, examples, and an evaluation harness for TypeScript and Python projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains MCP server planning, tool naming, response formats, pagination, and transport selection.
Provides TypeScript MCP SDK patterns with Zod schemas and structured tool responses.
Provides Python FastMCP patterns with Pydantic models and async API clients.
Includes guidance for authentication, error handling, rate limits, and DNS rebinding protection.
Includes an evaluation harness for testing MCP servers with XML question sets.
Shows quality checklists for implementation review before release.
limitations: It is a guide and helper script set, not a complete server generator.
Example endpoints and keys are placeholders and must be replaced before use.
The evaluation harness requires an Anthropic API key and sends evaluation data to Anthropic.
SDK details may need verification against the latest MCP documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan a New MCP Integration
use_cases.description: Map service APIs into clear MCP tools with names, schemas, response formats, and transport choices.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Server Quality
use_cases.description: Review tool descriptions, pagination, error messages, schemas, and annotations against MCP best practices.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agent Usefulness
use_cases.description: Create XML evaluation tasks and run the included harness to measure whether agents can complete realistic workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Server Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new MCP server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mcp-builder skill to plan an MCP server for my service. Identify tools, inputs, outputs, transports, and required authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mcp-builder skill to design MCP tool schemas for these API endpoints. Include validation constraints, pagination, annotations, and error behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Implementation Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mcp-builder skill to review my MCP server for tool naming, schema quality, response format, security, and maintainability issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create Evaluation Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mcp-builder skill to create realistic read-only evaluation questions for my MCP server and explain how to verify stable answers.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output_examples.output: A tool inventory grouped by workflow, with transport choice, authentication notes, pagination strategy, and schema requirements.

output_examples.input: Review this TypeScript MCP server design.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering naming, validation, structured responses, error messages, security controls, and missing tests.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation questions for a customer support MCP server.
output_examples.output: A set of read-only evaluation tasks with stable expected answers and notes about how each answer should be verified.

best_practices: Keep MCP tools focused, well named, and specific to the service domain.
Use schema validation, pagination, structured responses, and clear error messages for every tool.
Document authentication, permissions, rate limits, and transport security before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not expose broad tools that map directly to every API endpoint without workflow design.
Do not return unbounded result sets or verbose raw API payloads by default.
Do not run evaluations against sensitive production data without redaction and consent.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It guides design and implementation, then helps review and evaluate the result.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers TypeScript with the MCP SDK and Python with FastMCP patterns.

faq.question: Does it support remote MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses streamable HTTP for remote servers and stdio for local integrations.

faq.question: Can it test a server after implementation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an evaluation guide and a script for running XML-based evaluation tasks.

faq.question: What credentials are needed?
faq.answer: The evaluation harness needs an Anthropic API key. Your target service may require separate API credentials.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with private data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Evaluation results and tool outputs can be sent to Anthropic unless you modify the harness.
